skill.name: social-content
skill.description: Create, repurpose, schedule, and optimize social media content for LinkedIn, Twitter/X, Instagram, TikTok, and Facebook.
skill.summary: Plan platform-specific social posts, calendars, engagement tactics, and analytics-driven improvements.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: All static external-command findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences around social media templates and copy examples. The system-reconnaissance hits are ordinary marketing wording, not host or network reconnaissance. I added one medium semantic finding for guidance that recommends collecting hundreds of third-party posts with scraper tools.

remediation.suggestion: Replace scraper-based collection guidance with permission-based exports, manual sampling, or user-provided datasets, and add platform policy reminders.
Change the opening claim to say the skill advises on scheduling, unless an approved publishing integration actually exists.

semantic_findings.title: Large-Scale Social Platform Scraping Guidance
semantic_findings.description: The skill tells users to gather 500-1000+ posts and lists Apify and Phantom Buster scraper tools. This can encourage unauthorized platform scraping or collection of third-party content at scale.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Lines 620-628 explicitly describe collecting posts at scale and name automation scraper tools. The risk depends on user permissions and platform policy, so confidence is high but not absolute.

content.value_statement: Teams often lose time adapting one idea across social platforms. This skill turns goals, audience, and source content into platform-ready posts, calendars, and optimization plans.
actual_capabilities: Builds content pillars and platform strategies for LinkedIn, Twitter/X, Instagram, TikTok, and Facebook.
Drafts post templates, hooks, captions, threads, carousel outlines, and short video scripts.
Converts blogs, podcasts, videos, and interviews into platform-specific social posts.
Creates weekly calendars, batching plans, and scheduling guidance.
Defines engagement routines and metrics for iterative performance reviews.
limitations: Does not publish posts or connect to social scheduling tools by itself.
Does not verify current platform algorithms, trends, or policy changes.
Requires user-provided brand voice, audience, and performance data for best results.
Scraping competitor posts may require platform permission and legal review.

use_cases.title: Launch a founder-led content routine
use_cases.description: Turn founder insights into LinkedIn posts, Twitter/X threads, and weekly engagement actions.

use_cases.title: Repurpose long-form assets
use_cases.description: Convert blogs, podcasts, webinars, or videos into social posts for multiple channels.

use_cases.title: Improve content performance
use_cases.description: Use past post data to refine hooks, formats, posting times, and calls to action.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a LinkedIn Post
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for one platform-specific post.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create one LinkedIn post for this audience: [audience]. Goal: [goal]. Topic: [topic]. Use a [tone] voice and include one engagement question.

prompt_templates.title: Repurpose One Asset
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for adapting existing content.
prompt_templates.prompt: Repurpose this [blog, podcast, video, or webinar] into LinkedIn, Twitter/X, and Instagram content. Keep the main idea consistent but adapt each format.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Weekly Calendar
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced planning request for a multi-platform schedule.
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a one-week social content calendar for [brand]. Include platforms, post format, topic, hook angle, CTA, and suggested publishing window.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze Approved Examples
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced optimization using data the user is allowed to provide.
prompt_templates.prompt: Using only these posts or metrics I am allowed to use, identify hook patterns, format patterns, CTA patterns, and safe improvements for my next content cycle.

output_examples.input: Turn a product update into LinkedIn and Twitter/X content.
output: LinkedIn post opens with the customer problem, explains the update, and ends with a practical question.
Twitter/X thread starts with the outcome, breaks the update into benefits, and closes with a concise CTA.
Suggested tone is direct, useful, and specific to the target buyer.

output_examples.input: Create a weekly content plan for a B2B SaaS founder.
output: Monday focuses on an industry insight for LinkedIn and a short Twitter/X opinion post.
Wednesday turns a customer lesson into a story post and a carousel outline.
Friday reviews engagement data and tests a new hook format.

output_examples.input: Improve an Instagram caption for a carousel.
output: The revised caption starts with a clear problem statement.
The middle adds context for the carousel without repeating every slide.
The ending asks readers to save the post and share their next step.

best_practices: Provide audience, goal, platform, offer, and brand voice before asking for drafts.
Review every post for accuracy, compliance, and tone before publishing.
Use your own analytics to refine hooks, formats, timing, and CTAs.
anti_patterns: Asking for viral content without defining audience or business goal.
Cross-posting the same copy to every platform without adaptation.
Scraping or reusing third-party posts without permission or attribution.

faq.question: What platforms does this skill support?
faq.answer: It supports LinkedIn, Twitter/X, Instagram, TikTok, Facebook, and general social media planning.

faq.question: Can it publish or schedule posts?
faq.answer: No. It can plan schedules and write content, but it does not connect to publishing tools.

faq.question: Can it create a content calendar?
faq.answer: Yes. It can create weekly or monthly calendars with platform, format, topic, hook, and CTA guidance.

faq.question: Can it repurpose existing content?
faq.answer: Yes. It can turn blogs, podcasts, videos, interviews, and webinars into platform-specific social posts.

faq.question: Does it guarantee viral results?
faq.answer: No. It provides proven content patterns, but performance depends on audience fit, timing, quality, and platform changes.

faq.question: How should I use competitor examples safely?
faq.answer: Use only posts or metrics you are allowed to analyze. Do not copy protected content or collect personal data without permission.
